title: Recalibrate alert policy with rate-limiting and priority routing
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: After the recent capacity regression incident we observed sustained burn-rate oscillations that produced low-signal paging for the primary on-call. This ticket scopes a pragmatic policy overhaul: add a lightweight rate-limiter and priority-routing layer in front of burn-rate pagers, implement a short-term adaptive decay filter for spike-induced burns, and ship monitoring to validate reduced pager noise while preserving high-severity alerts.
background: During the 2026-01-30 regression event the burn-rate alerts caused repeated pages for transient capacity drops. Root cause mitigation reduced the underlying regressions, but alerting remained noisy. Current configuration: single global burn threshold with 5m evaluation window and immediate paging. We need to avoid loss of signal for real customer-impact events while cutting false positives from ephemeral spikes and correlated autoscaler chatter.
investigation_findings: >60% of pages in the last 90 days came from burn spikes shorter than 2 minutes
Many pages coincided with autoscaler churn during deployments (spike+decay pattern)
Existing aggregation groups are too coarse: cross-region failures produce duplicate pages
Current burn calculation does not weight error impact (all errors treated equally)
On-call feedback: frequent pages during low-traffic windows reduce ability to respond to high-impact alerts
proposed_changes: Deploy a rate-limiter proxy (alert-combiner) with per-oncall bucket and token-bucket smoothing to limit page frequency to 1 page / 10m for low-impact burns
Introduce priority-routing so high-impact burns (customer_impact==high OR >50% request loss) bypass smoothing and page immediately
Change burn evaluation: add transient-spike decay (exponential decay with half-life 90s) to reduce weight of <3m spikes
Split global burn groups by service+region+model to deduplicate correlated signals
Add weighted-burn metric that multiplies error count by customer_impact to avoid paging for low-impact background failures
Provide a gradual rollout: percentage rollout via feature flag for the alert-combiner, telemetry-only mode first, then soft-suppress, then hard-suppress
acceptance_criteria: Pager volume from burn-rate alerts reduces by >=60% during baseline non-incident windows (dashboard verification)
No regression in mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for high-impact incidents across a 30-day canary window
New alert-combiner service has 99.9% availability and <200ms median decision latency
All suppressed pages include a recovery breadcrumb and link to original raw signal for triage
Documentation updated for on-call runbook and escalation paths
